On June 15, 2013 06:33:24 PM EDT, Jiqiang Guo <guo...@gmail.com> wrote:
> http://www.openbugs.info/Examples/Volumeiii.html


Thanks. I hadn't realized they kept adding examples after
WinBUGS, so I was looking in the wrong doc.

I don't know what changed or if the to-do list was
just out of date, but the fire model's fitting just fine now.
200 iterations have R-hat under 1.1 for 4 chains with 15 or
so n_eff on all params matching those in OpenBUGS.

- Bob

parts:

figure out why it didn't work before!

converge compared to zero inits. I think this is
what Andrew wants

wanted to slightly reconfigure from zero inits for
these models. (For the record, our inits in (-2,2) work,
but they're painfully slow to adapt and converge compared to
zero inits. Sounds)

On June 17, 2013 06:14:09 PM EDT, Jiqiang Guo <guo...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Bob,
>
> Will you have a pull request for this example? Otherwise, I will update

> this example to use if / else statement instead of if_else functioI would like to take another pass at all the models,
but I'm still really tied up with other business at the moment.

So please go ahead and update all you can. I'm going to
make the lp__ change relatively soon (maybe not for 2.0 --- depends
how much time I get), so we'll need more updates then.

I'm amazed at how well all the models you coded work
and that we get exactly the same answers as BUGS up to MCMC
error (usually closer than that, even).

I did manage to get all the funshapes working, which was,
indeed, fun.

One thing I'd like to do is delete all the code that's
commented out in the models. I find it very distracting
when reading them.

I do think it's a good idea to have one basic translation
and one more idiomatic one. I don't quite know how we're
going to do this --- all the uses of step() seem really
clunky in the bugs models. Should we leave step() versions
in Stan, or just consider if_else() or just the comparison
as reasonable? That is, we can replace "step(a)" with "a > 0"
everywhere because (a > 0) returns 1 if a > 0 and 0 otherwise.

- Bob
